claims.head: Watch the Capitals’ puck management
claims.call: The Devils get at least their usual 7.8% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
claims.body: The Devils turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Capitals are the league’s worst at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Capitals.
claims.nums: New Jersey 3rd for chances off turnovers (7.8% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Washington 32nd for avoiding breakdowns
claims.gist: The Devils pounce on loose pucks, and the Capitals cough them up.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 4 games this season

check.measure: share of 5-on-5 expected goals within 5 seconds of winning the puck
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Devils’ goalie is in for some dangerous shots
claims.call: The Capitals’ average shot has at least their usual 6.7% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Devils have struggled to prevent dangerous shots, and the Capitals don’t waste many.
claims.nums: Washington 6th for shot quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · New Jersey 26th for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: The Capitals make their shots count, and the Devils allow dangerous ones.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 4 games this season

check.measure: the average shot’s chance of going in, by expected goals
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Capitals get in close; the Devils shoot from distance
claims.body: On shots from in close, Washington is near the top of the league and New Jersey is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
claims.nums: Shots from in close: Washington 8th, New Jersey 28th
claims.gist: The Capitals and the Devils sit at opposite ends for shots from in close.
claims.call: The Capitals take a bigger share of their shots from within 20 feet than the Devils.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 4 games this season

check.measure: share of 5-on-5 shots from within 20 feet
check.rule: held if the team comes out ahead by at least half its usual margin; partly if it comes out ahead by less; otherwise didn't happen

notes.text: C. Brown is out and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward. A. Mantha has taken his spot beside J. Bratt and J. Hughes.
M. Roy is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. T. Liljegren has taken his spot beside J. Chychrun.

WSH.head: Not an easy night for Washington
WSH.body: New Jersey has controlled the play far better over recent games and Washington has home ice. Washington can pull it off if they get good looks.

NJD.head: New Jersey has a lot going for them
NJD.body: New Jersey has controlled the play far better over recent games and Washington has home ice. Washington’s way back in is getting good looks.

story.head: Bratt’s favourite opponent
paras: The Capitals have won two in a row. The Devils are 2-2-0.
The Devils pounce on loose pucks, and the Capitals cough them up. The Capitals and the Devils sit at opposite ends for shots from in close.

items.text: Declan Chisholm faces his old team, Washington.
Jesper Bratt has a point in eight straight games against Washington.
Alex Ovechkin has six goals in ten games against New Jersey since 2023-24.
Matt Roy has missed the Capitals’ last two games.
